purpose: Every sign-in and every permission change on the platform leaves an audit receipt, and this brief writes that receipt and the code that emits and verifies it. The receipt's shape is IDENTITY-001's shared contract carried as written (docs/design/identity/briefs/IDENTITY-001.md:57): a version, a stable operation ID, the actor, the affected identity, the operation, a payload commitment and the log coordinate where the record sits, with one addition under a lead's ruling, the test tag of W3. It is signed by the service that performed the operation, never by the party it is about, because a claim must not be settable by the party being judged (P8, CN13). The signed event is the appended leaf, in the order the operations happened, and the receipt is returned beside it (IDENTITY-001.md:49, DIRECTORY-003 R2, CN14). The verifier lives in the lys CLI, offline, given only the log and the service's public key (W2, ADR-025), and refuses a receipt whose payload commitment does not match the leaf at its coordinate under the published CLI's one refusal class (A9, CN17). Receipts are for changes only; an answered permission check is never one (W1, ADR-024, CN15). A development install emits test receipts under a test key and a test tag that a real key never verifies (W3, ADR-026, CN16). This brief defines the common receipt and its verifier and replaces nothing: DIRECTORY-003 R2 (identity changes, docs/design/directory/briefs/DIRECTORY-003.md:64-70), DIRECTORY-004 ID001_LINK_AUDIT (provider links and unlinks, docs/design/directory/briefs/DIRECTORY-004.md:41) and DIRECTORY-006 GRANT_AUDIT (grants, docs/design/directory/briefs/DIRECTORY-006.md:100) keep emitting their receipts inside their own walls, unedited (A1).
task: Five rows, in order: R1 the contract document (2 hours), R2 the receipt crate and verifier core (4 hours), R3 the lys CLI verifier (3 hours), R4 the sign-in receipts the directory service emits (4 hours), R5 the development-install proof (2 hours): 15 focused implementer hours, a new increment beside IDENTITY-001's ceiling (CN7), not inside it. R1 is documents only and lands first; R2 and R3 start only when IDENTITY-EVENTS.md is on main with its version, typed payloads, named commitment hash and recorded review (blocked_by); R4 and R5 start only when DIRECTORY-003 has landed. What stands on main and is not reopened: the shared contract (IDENTITY-001.md:57), the audit-record wording of docs/design/identity/LIFECYCLE-STATES-2026-09-22.md:40-44, and the three acts that stay Tom's, publishing lys-anchor, generating a production key and emitting a receipt outside a test (docs/design/lys-anchor/DECISIONS.md:333-335). The rulings realised: W1 (receipts for changes only; the access record is step 2's), W2 (the verifier in the lys CLI, offline), W3 (test receipts under a test key and a test tag), and the settled answers A1 to A12, with A8 standing where it corrects A7. Development record, kept here because the pipeline appends the dev block later: main corrected A7. DIRECTORY-003 R1 says that in step 1 the only caller that may register a person is the configured administrator and a first sign-in registers nobody (DIRECTORY-003.md:39), so in step 1 a first sign-in leaves a sign-in receipt, or a refusal receipt when the issuer-subject is bound to no registered identity, and the administrator's register act leaves the register receipt; A7's one register event on first sign-in is ADR-011's proposal for step 2's self-registration (LIFECYCLE-STATES-2026-09-22.md:34) and applies only when a brief brings that. Where a count could be argued (how many leaves a scenario leaves, how many cases a tamper matrix holds, how many refusals a leg asserts) it is decided by rule in this brief, as the lead decided the E10 counts for the sibling briefs tonight, and the legs assert those numbers. Every code row is red first: its first commit adds its test file alone and the named tests fail; its second commit makes them pass. No wall clock anywhere in the new code: every time value a test needs is injected by the harness. No name of a person and no date inside code. Every path is relative to the repository root. The shared, pre-existing files of the published CLI this brief touches (crates/lys/src/cli.rs, crates/lys/src/main.rs, crates/lys/src/commands/error.rs, crates/lys/src/commands/log/mod.rs, crates/lys/Cargo.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock) are owned by no brief; DIRECTORY-002 also edits the first three, and whichever row lands second rebases onto the first's additions. Anything under crates/lys-identity/ is DIRECTORY-003's wall and is not edited.

requirements.title: Write the audit receipt contract as it stands, the emitter of every operation, and what the envelope review must carry
requirements.spec: Documents only. THE SYSTEM SHALL add docs/design/identity/AUDIT-RECEIPT.md holding, in this order: (1) the contract sentence of docs/design/identity/briefs/IDENTITY-001.md:57 word for word, 'Audit receipts carry a version, stable operation ID, actor, affected identity, operation, payload commitment and resulting log coordinate/checkpoint. Secrets and whole context objects are excluded. Exact signed encoding is reviewed before use, not frozen by this draft.', and the one field added under a lead's ruling, the test tag (W3), with the rule that no other field is added without a lead's ruling; (2) the signer rule: the service that performed the operation signs, never the party the receipt is about, and a verifier is given the service's public key and never takes a key carried in the receipt as its authority (CN13); (3) the leaf rule: the signed event is the appended leaf, appended in the order the operations happened, and the receipt is returned beside it carrying the coordinate the append yielded and the payload commitment, and is never itself appended (IDENTITY-001.md:49, DIRECTORY-003.md:64-66, CN14); (4) the emitter table, one row per operation, each naming exactly one emitting brief or row: an identity moving between lifecycle states, DIRECTORY-003 R5; a person or agent being registered and a display-profile change, DIRECTORY-003 R1 (A12); a provider being linked to a person and unlinked from one, DIRECTORY-004 ID001_LINK_AUDIT through its outbox and DIRECTORY-003 R4's receiver (A12); a grant being given or taken away, DIRECTORY-006 GRANT_AUDIT, whose payload waits on the grant representation that is OPEN for Tom (docs/design/directory/DESIGN.md:58, A6), so the common receipt commits only to the seven fields and treats the payload commitment as a commitment over whatever representation is settled; a sign-in the directory service records and a sign-in it refuses after Rauthy authenticated the person, this brief's R4 (A4, A11); an agent being provisioned, no row and no receipt of its own, because provisioned is a view over grants and a handle and not a transition (LIFECYCLE-STATES-2026-09-22.md:26-28), so it shows as the agent's register transition and then each grant given to it (A5); the table states that the words' list names operations that must emit one and not the only ones, since IDENTITY-001's rule makes one signed event both the change and its audit record (IDENTITY-001.md:44, A12); (5) the step-1 sign-in boundary: the directory service refuses exactly one kind of authenticated sign-in, an issuer-subject Rauthy authenticated that is bound to no identity the administrator registered, and that refusal leaves the refusal receipt; a suspended or retired identity produces no state-based refusal receipt because state is recorded and not enforced in step 1 (CN11, DIRECTORY-003.md:122), and suspension semantics stay OPEN for Tom; the step-2 refusals arrive with enforcement (A11); a first sign-in in step 1 registers nobody, so it leaves a sign-in receipt or the refusal receipt and the administrator's register act leaves the register receipt, and the document records that main corrected A7 this way (A8); Rauthy's own refusals, a bad password or a failed provider callback, are out of scope because Rauthy's native events are asynchronous and severity-filtered (IDENTITY-001.md:44) and a signing key inside Rauthy is a fork change under ADR-009 that no brief of this repository makes (A4); (6) the changes-only rule: a permission check that is answered and changes nothing is not a receipt; when step 2 brings enforcement, allows and refusals go to a separate access record that step 2 defines, refusals always, allows decided with step 2, so nobody later puts high-volume checks into the signed receipt log (W1, CN15); (7) the test-receipt rule: a development install emits test receipts, signed with a test key and carrying the test tag, inside IDENTITY-001's development isolation, and never performs the act docs/design/lys-anchor/DECISIONS.md:335 reserves; the verifier refuses a test-tagged receipt by name unless given the test key explicitly, and a real key never verifies a test receipt (W3, CN16); (8) the verifier's order and refusal classes, as R2 and R3 build them (A9, CN17); (9) the list of what docs/design/identity/IDENTITY-EVENTS.md must carry before R2 to R5 start, as inputs to DIRECTORY-003's joint review and not as edits: the envelope version field the verifier is written against, the typed payloads, the named commitment hash (SHA-256 named explicitly, never confused with a BLAKE3 content address, IDENTITY-001.md:49), the test tag, the sign-in and sign-in-refusal operations in the vocabulary with the affected identity empty and the issuer and subject in the typed payload for a refusal of an unbound subject, and the recorded review (A3, ADR-025); and (10) the release rule: a lys release carrying the verifier is a separate, deliberate act after IDENTITY-EVENTS.md's version is ratified and recorded, never before, under CLAUDE.md:78-80; landing on main publishes nothing (A10, CN18). The document SHALL NOT restate any of these as a new decision, SHALL NOT fix an encoding, tag or content type, SHALL NOT edit any IDENTITY-001 file, the lifecycle states document or IDENTITY-EVENTS.md, and SHALL NOT decide anything the design records as OPEN for Tom.

requirements.title: Build the receipt crate: the typed receipt of the shared shape and the verifier core, with one refusal class
requirements.spec: THE SYSTEM SHALL add the wholly new crate crates/lys-receipt (its exact file manifest is this row's files list, reviewed at sign-off, CN9) as a library that reads a receipt of the shared shape and verifies it against a log and a key, and that signs nothing outside its own test harness. It depends on lys-core for Ed25519 verification and SHA-256 and on lys-log-store for the LeafStore trait (crates/lys-log-store/src/store.rs:120-141); it SHALL NOT change lys-core, lys-log-store or any published wire format, and lys-core gains no identity concept. crates/lys-receipt/src/receipt.rs SHALL define the typed receipt exactly as docs/design/identity/IDENTITY-EVENTS.md writes it at its ratified version: version, operation ID, actor, affected identity, operation, payload commitment, log coordinate, the test tag and the signature, parsed from JSON by a function that refuses by name, ReceiptError::MalformedReceipt naming what was malformed, any input that is not JSON, lacks a field, or carries a version other than the one the crate is written against; the operation is read as a string of IDENTITY-EVENTS.md's vocabulary and SHALL NOT be enumerated by the crate (A12). crates/lys-receipt/src/verify.rs SHALL verify in this order: (a) WHERE the receipt carries the test tag, THE SYSTEM SHALL consult only the test key, and IF no test key was given THEN it SHALL refuse with ReceiptError::NeedsTestKey, whose message is 'test-tagged receipt: supply the test key', before any cryptography; WHERE the receipt carries no test tag, it SHALL consult only the verifier key and never the test key, so a real key never verifies a test receipt and a test key never verifies a receipt as real (W3, CN16); (b) the signature over the receipt's signed bytes against the consulted key's Ed25519 public key; (c) the coordinate lies within the store's extent; (d) the named commitment hash of the leaf bytes at that coordinate equals the receipt's payload commitment. Every failure of (b), (c) or (d) SHALL collapse to the one refusal ReceiptError::VerificationFailed, whose message is 'receipt verification failed: invalid receipt, signature, coordinate or leaf', so tamper classes are indistinguishable from the output (crates/lys/src/commands/log/verify.rs:7-14, A9, CN17). On success it SHALL return the log's origin, the leaf index, the operation, the operation ID, the affected identity and whether the receipt is a test receipt, and nothing else. THE SYSTEM SHALL read the log through LeafStore::leaf and LeafStore::extent only, SHALL NOT call Log::open (crates/lys-log-store/src/log.rs:99, which may write a repaired pin) or append, and SHALL NOT write to the log directory. Debug and Display of the receipt and of every error SHALL NOT contain the leaf bytes or the signature bytes. The crate SHALL NOT read a wall clock: every time value in its tests is injected by the harness in crates/lys-receipt/tests/support/mod.rs, which also holds the harness signer over generated test keys, the fixture log builder and the tamper table, and is never compiled into the library.
acceptance: Leg 1 of 7, rcpt_accept: five operations committed in order into a fixture log occupy leaves 0 to 4 in that order and yield exactly 5 receipts, all 5 accepted, each report naming the fixture's origin, its leaf index and its operation; cargo test -p lys-receipt --test receipt_verify rcpt_accept prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'.

Leg 2 of 7, rcpt_tamper: a table of exactly 9 cases, one each for a changed version, operation ID, actor, affected identity, operation, payload commitment and coordinate, one flipped signature byte, and one receipt signed by the affected identity's own test key instead of the service's, yields 9 ReceiptError::VerificationFailed and 0 acceptances, and the 9 Display strings are equal to each other and to 'receipt verification failed: invalid receipt, signature, coordinate or leaf'; cargo test -p lys-receipt --test receipt_verify rcpt_tamper prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'.

Leg 3 of 7, rcpt_leaf: a receipt correctly signed by the service key whose coordinate names a leaf holding different bytes, and a correctly signed receipt whose coordinate is the store's extent, yield exactly 2 ReceiptError::VerificationFailed with the same Display string as leg 2, and the test counts 2 refusals from 2 cases; cargo test -p lys-receipt --test receipt_verify rcpt_leaf prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'.

Leg 4 of 7, rcpt_testtag: four cases: a test-tagged receipt with no test key returns ReceiptError::NeedsTestKey whose Display contains 'supply the test key'; the same receipt with the test key is accepted with the test flag true; a test-tagged receipt signed with the verifier key, given both keys, returns VerificationFailed; an untagged receipt signed with the test key, given both keys, returns VerificationFailed; the test asserts 1 NeedsTestKey, 1 acceptance and 2 VerificationFailed; cargo test -p lys-receipt --test receipt_verify rcpt_testtag prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'.

Leg 5 of 7, rcpt_shape: three inputs, bytes that are not JSON, a JSON object lacking the operation field, and a receipt whose version is not the crate's, each return ReceiptError::MalformedReceipt whose Display begins 'malformed receipt' and names the missing field or the version; the test asserts 3 refusals from 3 cases and that none of the three Display strings equals leg 2's; cargo test -p lys-receipt --test receipt_verify rcpt_shape prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'.

Leg 6 of 7, rcpt_redact: with a leaf whose bytes hold the marker 'fixture-marker-0' and a receipt whose signature bytes are known, the Debug and Display renderings of the receipt and of each of the three error variants contain the marker 0 times and the signature's hex 0 times; cargo test -p lys-receipt --test receipt_verify rcpt_redact prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'.

Leg 7 of 7, rcpt_clock and the mapping: rg -n 'SystemTime::now|Utc::now|Local::now|Instant::now' crates/lys-receipt prints nothing; rg -c 'fn \w*rcpt_(accept|tamper|leaf|testtag|shape|redact)(_|\b)' crates/lys-receipt/tests/receipt_verify.rs prints 6; and on the row's first commit cargo test -p lys-receipt --test receipt_verify fails to compile or prints '0 passed' with the six names listed as failed.

requirements.title: Add lys log verify receipt to the CLI, offline, from the log and the key alone
requirements.spec: THE SYSTEM SHALL add the subcommand lys log verify receipt --receipt <file> --dir <log directory> --verifier-key <string> [--test-key <string>] [--json] to the published CLI (W2, ADR-025), implemented in the new file crates/lys/src/commands/log/receipt.rs and declared as the Receipt variant of LogVerifyCommand in crates/lys/src/cli.rs (beside Inclusion and Consistency, crates/lys/src/cli.rs:438-480), dispatched from crates/lys/src/main.rs beside the two existing verify arms (crates/lys/src/main.rs:66-75), with the module line added to crates/lys/src/commands/log/mod.rs and the lys-receipt dependency added to crates/lys/Cargo.toml. It SHALL need no running service: it reads the receipt file (capped at 16 MiB as the other artifacts are, crates/lys/src/commands/log/verify.rs:29-32), opens the log directory through lys-log-store's FileLeafStore::open (crates/lys-log-store/src/file.rs:165) as a LeafStore and never as a Log, parses each key string with NoteVerifierKey::from_spec (crates/lys-core/src/checkpoint/verifier_key.rs:92), the same ORIGIN+KEYID_HEX+KEY_BASE64 form the other verify commands take, and calls crates/lys-receipt's verifier. Refusals keep the published discipline: pre-crypto and actionable, each named on its own, CliError::JsonParse with what 'receipt' for a malformed receipt file, CliError::Trust for a malformed --verifier-key or --test-key string, and the new CliError::ReceiptNeedsTestKey, whose message is 'test-tagged receipt: supply the test key with --test-key', for a test-tagged receipt presented without --test-key; every cryptographic or structural failure collapses to the new CliError::ReceiptVerificationFailed, whose message is 'receipt verification failed: invalid receipt, signature, coordinate or leaf', one message per artifact class as CliError::LogInclusionVerificationFailed is (crates/lys/src/commands/error.rs:189-196, A9, CN17). Both variants are appended to crates/lys/src/commands/error.rs; no existing variant or message changes. On success it SHALL print, through the Emitter, 'receipt verified', the origin, the leaf index, the operation, the operation ID, the affected identity and 'test receipt: true' or 'test receipt: false', and exit 0; every refusal exits 1 with its message on stderr. It SHALL NOT write to the log directory, SHALL NOT change the behaviour or output of lys log verify inclusion or consistency, and SHALL NOT publish any crate: the lys release carrying this subcommand is a separate act after IDENTITY-EVENTS.md's version is ratified (A10, CN18).
acceptance: Leg 1 of 6, rcli_accept: a fixture log directory, a receipt from crates/lys-receipt's harness and the service's key string: the binary exits 0 and its stdout contains 'receipt verified', the fixture origin, 'leaf index' with the receipt's index, the operation and 'test receipt: false'; with --json the same fields appear as JSON keys; cargo test -p lys --test receipt_tests rcli_accept prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'.

Leg 2 of 6, rcli_tamper: the 9 tamper cases of R2 leg 2 and the 2 leaf cases of R2 leg 3, 11 in all, each exit 1 with stderr identical across all 11 and equal to 'receipt verification failed: invalid receipt, signature, coordinate or leaf' plus the CLI's error prefix; the test counts 11 refusals from 11 cases; cargo test -p lys --test receipt_tests rcli_tamper prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'.

Leg 3 of 6, rcli_precrypto: five cases: a receipt file that is not JSON and one lacking a field each exit 1 with stderr naming 'receipt' and the file path; a malformed --verifier-key and a malformed --test-key each exit 1 with stderr naming the key string as malformed; a test-tagged receipt without --test-key exits 1 with stderr containing 'supply the test key with --test-key'; none of the five stderr strings equals leg 2's; the test counts 5 refusals from 5 cases; cargo test -p lys --test receipt_tests rcli_precrypto prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'.

Leg 4 of 6, rcli_test: a test-tagged receipt with --test-key exits 0 and stdout contains 'test receipt: true'; the same receipt with --verifier-key set to the key that signed it and --test-key set to another key exits 1 with leg 2's stderr, so a real key never verifies a test receipt; the test counts 1 acceptance and 1 refusal; cargo test -p lys --test receipt_tests rcli_test prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'.

requirements.title: Emit the sign-in and sign-in-refusal receipts from the directory service, for changes only
requirements.spec: WHEN Rauthy has authenticated a person and the directory service resolves the issuer-subject to an identity the administrator registered, THE SYSTEM SHALL commit one signed event of operation sign-in through the landed lys-identity commit path (DIRECTORY-003 R2), attesting the authenticated person and their provenance as the actor and naming that identity as the affected identity, and return the receipt beside the appended leaf. WHEN the issuer-subject is bound to no registered identity, THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse the sign-in by name, SignInRefusal::UnboundSubject with message prefix sign_in_unbound_subject, register nobody, and commit one signed event of operation sign-in-refused whose affected identity is empty and whose typed payload carries the issuer and subject, returning its receipt (A8, A11). In step 1 this is the only kind of authenticated sign-in the service refuses: WHILE an identity is suspended or retired, THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT refuse its sign-in on state and SHALL leave the sign-in receipt, since state is recorded and not enforced (CN11, DIRECTORY-003.md:122); the step-2 refusals arrive with enforcement and suspension semantics stay OPEN for Tom. A read of a record and any permission question that is answered SHALL NOT commit an event or leave a receipt (W1, CN15).
